{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABYqvu1Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhCPsn8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 31, "title": "Make the PC-VAN interface immersive: hide meta commentary, move controls into Settings, and use period-style Japanese terminal typography", "body": "## Problem

The current PC-VAN experience repeatedly breaks immersion. On connection and throughout MAIN/SIG/forum screens, normal output includes long provenance explanations such as "創作", "再構成", "未確認", "[D / reconstructed]" and source URLs. Below the terminal, multiple AI, user, display, backup and offline controls remain visibly stacked (even when individual details are collapsed). The current generic-looking Japanese font also feels unlike a 1990s PC text terminal.

The desired default experience is **entering PC-VAN**, not reading an explanatory prototype or using a dashboard. Preserve honest provenance, but show it **on demand**, not during everyday operation.

## Expected outcome

Opening or reconnecting presents a clean PC-VAN-style terminal and navigable period-inspired text, with very little surrounding chrome. Ordinary menus, forum listing/reading, and help messages are concise and contain no unsolicited historical/reconstruction commentary or source URLs. A small, accessible **設定 / Options** trigger opens a consolidated settings panel/dialog containing secondary controls and a discoverable **このシステムについて / Sources & limitations** section. Use typography that is visually closer to a Japanese PC terminal (sharper, compact, cell-aligned Japanese bitmap/monospace styling) without introducing illegible text or unlicensed font assets.

**Preserve all original behavior** (keyboard navigation, forums, posting, AI, display-speed effects, backup/restore, offline controls, data retention, GitHub Pages). This is one focused UI/UX Issue, not a replacement of historical evidence or core logic.

## Context

Current `main` (reinspect before coding):
- `src/connection.ts` includes a four-line simulated connection greeting explaining that text and timing are invented.
- `src/navigation.ts` mixes navigable menu data with provenance categories, source URLs and caveats inside `renderMain()`, `forumNotice()`, `renderForum()`, service screens and helper prompts. These appear repeatedly, sometimes on every article read.
- `src/terminal.ts` displays "1996年頃の MAIN（暫定）· ローカル再構成", "ブラウザー内セッション", permanently visible speed controls, and a separate display-controls section.
- `src/main.ts` mounts the human-member/post composer, AI, JSON backup and offline settings into the same page. See `src/ai/controls.ts`, `src/storage/controls.ts` and `src/offline/controls.ts`. Existing `<details>` sections do not sufficiently hide secondary UI because their summaries remain below the terminal.
- `src/style.css` defaults to `"Noto Sans Mono CJK JP", "BIZ UDGothic", "MS Gothic", "Osaka-Mono", monospace` with relatively roomy `16px / 1.65` typography. Actual installed fonts and widths vary by OS.
- [Historical evidence and uncertainty](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md) must remain available and accurate, including the fact that some menu prompts/paths are reconstructed and archived demonstration posts are fictional. **Do not delete evidence data or falsely claim historical accuracy.** Move details into on-demand About/Sources UI and existing documentation instead.
- The preceding terminal design/streaming change is covered by [#29](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/29); preserve its rendering speed, skip, theme and reduced-motion behavior.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), the [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), and [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md). Newly authored Issue/PR/docs text is English; Japanese app text stays Japanese.

### Design directions

- **Normal mode**: display only meaningful connection text, historical-style menus, selections, errors, post content, short command prompts and necessary notices. Prefer immediate entry to MAIN after a restrained connection effect. Keep short operational HELP, not repeated authenticity disclaimers. No URLs, evidence-category codes or "(再構成)" suffixes in ordinary terminal output.
- **Options**: a discreet `設定` button in terminal chrome opens a single native `<dialog>` or equivalently accessible settings overlay. Organize existing **display/theme/speed**, **human handle/member**, **local AI**, **JSON backup/restore**, **offline/storage**, **help**, and **About/Sources** controls in clearly named groups. Reuse the current controls and event wiring rather than reimplementing logic. Avoid persistent rows of settings panels beneath the terminal; reserve the viewport for the terminal.
- **About/Sources**: explicitly describe the browser-only reconstruction, historically confirmed vs provisional behavior and AI/demo post provenance, and link to the research docs. This is the place for caveats and sources, available without leaving the session. Mark synthetic demo posts/AI identity where discoverability is necessary (e.g. author details or About), but never imply fictional output came from a real historical user.
- **Typography**: aim for a crisp, compact Japanese PC/PC-98-era text feeling, with appropriate locally available Gothic/monospace fallbacks and consistent full-width/half-width cells. Prefer a carefully ordered local/system-font stack; a freely licensed bundled bitmap-style Japanese font is acceptable **only if** its license explicitly permits redistribution and the asset is reasonably sized. No unauthorized proprietary NEC bitmap/font extraction, font downloads from random mirrors, external font CDN or broken fallbacks. Expose a legible fallback where authentic-looking pixel type is unavailable. Avoid overengineered font-loading infrastructure.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Startup, reconnect and MAIN menus render without any unsolicited `創作`, `再構成`, `暫定`, `未確認`, `reconstructed`, evidence markers, source URLs or repeated tutorial paragraphs. Retain functional prompts and a short usable connection status, and never show an empty/ambiguous screen. Check SIG directory, forum list, individual post, service-unavailable and disconnect paths too.
- [ ] Normal HELP and error text are concise and functional, without long provenance comments. Keep honest descriptions for *actual* unsupported functionality (e.g. OLT cannot be used); do not disguise an unavailable service as functional or invent period-verified screens.
- [ ] Historical provenance, differing eras, fabricated bridge controls, fictional demo posts and local AI-origin information remain accurate and discoverable under `設定 → このシステムについて / 出典・制約` (or equivalent). Preserve original fixture metadata, sources and research documentation; do not silently erase evidence or claim the UI is an exact historical replica.
- [ ] The ordinary viewport is dominated by the terminal. Only a discreet settings trigger and minimal essential terminal/status controls are present outside the text screen. Default load shows **none of the standalone display/member/AI/backup/offline settings sections or their summary rows** below the terminal. Preserve the built-in output-speed/skip workflow with access from Settings and/or a small unobtrusive control if needed.
- [ ] The Settings overlay opens/closes via keyboard and pointer, has an accessible name, logical tab order, visible focus, Escape/close support, and returns focus to the previously focused element or terminal input. Avoid focus conflicts with existing composer dialogs; do not nest native dialogs improperly or break Japanese IME submission. Allow setting a member, writing a post, loading/canceling AI, downloading/restoring JSON and opting into offline cache using the original behavior.
- [ ] Show actionable success/errors and progress **inside Settings when Settings is open** without permanently cluttering the terminal. For background AI activity or data errors, preserve a concise accessible indication/way to inspect details after Settings closes; do not silently hide failures.
- [ ] Use a clearly intentional Japanese PC-terminal font presentation (smaller/tighter line height and glyph rendering where appropriate), prioritizing Japanese legibility and actual monospaced cell alignment: full-width kana/kanji, ASCII, half-width kana, punctuation, spaces and the MAIN two-column layout must not drift, clip or overlap across common fallback configurations. Do not falsely label a modern font as a verified original PC-VAN font.
- [ ] Keep font/theme/zoom responsiveness usable on desktop and mobile. Text selection, horizontal scrolling, screen readers, text scaling and `prefers-reduced-motion` remain supported; no mandatory external font requests. Document any bundled font licensing if such a font is introduced.
- [ ] Existing application data/settings persist and import/export identically. No migration losses; terminal output streaming/skip/downloads, historical command routing, posting/replies, AI persona controls, cached offline shell and deployment under `/pcvan/` continue to work.
- [ ] Add or update Playwright tests for clean startup and ordinary menu/article output, About discoverability, default-hidden settings, modal keyboard/focus/Escape behavior, existing controls functioning inside it, old-state persistence, Japanese menu alignment and fallback fonts, mobile viewport, and no regression to speed/AI/offline workflows. Use stubs for GPU/model work. Run `npm test`, build and applicable whitespace/link checks; report actual results.

## Optional validation

Visual comparison with accessible screenshots of 1990s Japanese PC text terminals and subjective feedback from experienced PC-VAN users are helpful but not pre-merge gates. A native bitmap-style font can be explored only when redistribution rights and browser performance are clear.

## Required post-merge verification

None required for merge approval. This is a client-side behavior/UI change verifiable in the production build before merge; public GitHub Pages publication can be monitored separately under the existing workflow.
